mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO rise > 1% does not correlate with subsequent economic strength.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) YoY is below 2%, the real interest rate is positive, signaling a favorable monetary environment for equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the specified conditions do not correlate with subsequent positive equity performance.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increase > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the specified labor market conditions do not correlate with subsequent positive equity performance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals strengthening demand in the housing sector, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent positive economic sentiment.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 1% YoY and Industrial Production (INDPRO) is declining, it signals a supply-side recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the specified conditions do not correlate with subsequent negative equity performance.
